patent.title: Magnetic field sensor with ferromagnetic thin layers having magnetically antiparallel polarized components
patent.family_note: US counterpart of Grünberg / KFA Jülich DE priority (1988-06-16) for a multilayer magnetic-field sensor using ferromagnetic thin layers with antiparallel magnetization components separated by a nonferromagnetic interlayer of thickness below the conduction-electron mean free path. Package B early ledger uses grant-date T0 only; IBM 1997 commercial GMR/spin-valve HDD read heads and later areal-density success are excluded from this historical state. Related Fert PRL 1988 and Grünberg PRB 1989 papers are used only as pre-T0 GMR scientific platform context. Contemporaneous ~1990 anisotropic MR (AMR) heads are not treated as embodiments of this patent.

knowledge_origin.description: Public patent record identifies Peter Grünberg inventorship and Kernforschungsanlage Jülich (public research institute) ownership of the antiparallel multilayer magnetic-field sensor architecture.

technology.problem: Prior thin-film magnetoresistive sensors relying on anisotropic magnetoresistance produced only small resistance changes (e.g., ~few percent in Permalloy), limiting signal/noise for reading weak fields from magnetic data storage media.
technology.mechanism: Magnetic-field sensor stack of at least two ferromagnetic layers separated by a nonferromagnetic intermediate layer arranged so the ferromagnetic layers have antiparallel magnetization components; spin-dependent interface scattering yields magnetoresistance changes substantially larger than anisotropic MR systems without antiparallel alignment / proper interlayer (thickness less than conduction-electron mean free path).
technology.comparison_baseline: Anisotropic magnetoresistance thin-film sensors (e.g., Permalloy) with small MR ratio; multilayer stacks lacking antiparallel magnetization components or lacking an appropriate nonferromagnetic interlayer for spin-dependent scattering.

value_carriers.name: GMR / spin-valve magnetic HDD read-sensor platform (aspirational at T0; no marketed GMR carrier confirmed)
value_carriers.description: Pre-T0 Fert/Grünberg GMR science and the 1990 patent's claimed magnetic-data-storage read-sensor architecture demonstrate a high-sensitivity multilayer MR option, but at T0=1990-08-14 no public exact-patent mapping to a marketed GMR HDD read head is used in this ledger. Contemporaneous AMR heads are out of scope as embodiments.

gaps.description: At T0=1990-08-14 there is no confirmed exact-patent → marketed GMR HDD / magnetic-storage read-head carrier link in this ledger. Lab/device architecture and claimed magnetic-data-storage uses are not implemented as a public commercial GMR carrier here.
needed_evidence: license / supply schedule tying this grant to a marketed GMR head

gaps.description: No public T0 evidence attributes royalty, incremental HDD revenue, or cost/performance economics to this exact patent.

V0.7 can record R0 plus spintronic / magnetoresistance differentiation, but has no structured field for early option/future-value horizon that is decision-relevant precisely when realization is still R0/R1.
needed_evidence: explicit separation of option signals from realized R-stage

notes: Package B early-stage option retrospective #4 (spintronics / magnetic data-storage sensing; diversifies beyond mRNA life science, OLED organic display, and LIB energy-storage electrochemistry). T0=grant date 1990-08-14 stops at R0: Jülich public-institute patent + Fert PRL 1988 / Grünberg PRB 1989 GMR platform + patent claimed magnetic-storage read-sensor option signals exist, but no marketed exact-patent GMR carrier is recorded. IBM 1997 commercial GMR/spin-valve heads, later HDD areal-density success, and 2007 Nobel narratives are post-T0 and must not be backfilled into this ledger.
